core.title: Declare coverage exceptions only through allow-lists or in-progress status
core.given: A plan artifact (wagon, feature or WMBT) intentionally does not satisfy full coverage
core.when: the planner records that coverage gap
core.then: Declare the exception only through the matching coverage-exception allow-list entry or by marking the artifact with the stack's in-progress status — never leave the gap undeclared.
prefer: List wagons that are utility, shared or under development in the allow-list for wagons not placed in any train.
List deprecated or experimental features in the allow-list for features no wagon/WMBT references (orphaned features).
List draft/placeholder WMBTs in the allow-list for WMBTs without acceptance.

Mark genuinely unfinished artifacts with the stack's in-progress status; that status exempts them from full coverage only for the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope.
avoid: Leaving a coverage gap with no allow-list entry and no in-progress status.
Allow-listing an artifact in a list whose use case does not fit it (e.g. putting a finished, live wagon in the list for wagons not in any train).
Marking finished artifacts in-progress just to silence coverage checks, or assuming the status exempts from coverage findings outside its realization-defined exemption scope.
core.why: Coverage checks are strict; explicit, recorded exceptions keep intentional gaps visible and reviewable instead of hiding real missing coverage.
evidence: Every coverage gap reported by the detector maps to an entry under the matching coverage-exception allow-list key or to an artifact carrying the in-progress status.
Status exemptions are applied only to the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope.
Each allow-list entry fits its list's use case (utility/shared/under-development wagons; deprecated/experimental features; draft/placeholder WMBTs).
verification: Strict disposition: every coverage gap a check reports must be closed or matched by a declared exception — an allow-list entry in the list whose documented use case fits, or the artifact's in-progress status; an undeclared gap remains a violation.
An allow-list entry excepts a gap only when it sits in the list whose documented use case matches the artifact's situation; the check verifies each entry's use-case fit.
The in-progress status exempts only the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope; every other coverage check still applies to the artifact.

The concrete allow-list keys and the status literal are stack data supplied through the profile; which findings the status exempts is rule-specific disposition defined by this rule's realization, not profile data, and the finding ids of this rule are realization details named generically here.

values: artifact status set to or from the in-progress value

fires: Planner adds a utility/shared/under-development wagon that is intentionally not placed in any train.
Planner keeps a deprecated or experimental feature that no wagon/WMBT references.
Planner authors a draft or placeholder WMBT that has no acceptance yet.
A coverage check reports a gap and the planner intends to exempt rather than close it.
doesNotFire: Planner adds a wagon to a train, or a WMBT with full acceptance coverage — no exception is needed.
Code-only changes that touch no plan artifact or coverage config.

The idiom group exists for exactly such stack constructs behind a neutral concept.

proposedKeys.meaning: The plan-artifact status value that marks genuinely unfinished (in-progress) work.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key covers a plan-artifact status value marking unfinished work; enforcement.suppression_marker is a time-boxed rule suppression in source, not an artifact status, and no roles/layout key describes artifact status values. The exemption scope is deliberately excluded: which findings a status exempts is per-rule disposition that stays with each rule's realization, not stack-wide profile data.

neutralityNotes: Wagon, train, feature, WMBT and acceptance are treated as stack-neutral ATDD plan vocabulary (they are parameters of the closed vocabulary's layout and urn groups), so the core keeps them; only the concrete config keys (coverage.exceptions.*), the path globs / file-name patterns, the status literal (status: draft), and the finding ids (COVERAGE-PLAN-2.1/2.4) and term ids are realization-specific. The allow-list mechanism and the in-progress status representation have no vocabulary entry, so two idiom keys are proposed and also listed in profileRequirements. Per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys boundary, idiom.coverage_status_exemption carries only the status representation (status: draft); the exemption-scope list — which coverage findings the status exempts — is rule-specific disposition defined by this rule's realization, stated generically in core verification and kept exactly (with its finding ids) in bunOnly, never in the profile. The Bun activation fact names 'layer' and 'path_glob' were mapped to the neutral fact vocabulary as 'role' (plan_artifact) and 'file_kind' (plan_artifact, config). fires/doesNotFire were carried verbatim because they are already plan-level and stack-neutral. Instantiating the core with the Bun profile values plus the bunOnly items reproduces bun.json's obligation exactly: no exception path, use-case condition, or scope limit was dropped, and no new obligation was added.
